en:
So it's finally my turn.
I'm Makoto Shindo, third-year.
Nice to meet you all.
The story I'm gonna tell has to do with playing cards.
Cards.
There's nobody who's never played cards, right?{p}{a}, do you like playing cards?
I like them
I hate them
Neither, really

Just fifty-three cards, and there are so many different ways to play.
You can play alone, and you can play with a big group.
They don't take up any space, and all you need is the cards.
And you get so much fun out of them.
Games have come a long way lately, but if you ask me, nothing beats cards.
Whoever came up with them was a real genius.
I seriously respect them for it.
And then there's the fifty-third card.
That one really makes it.
The one they call the joker.
That thing makes cards so much more fun.
Just throwing the joker in opens up a whole lot more ways to play.
It's a magic card, no doubt about it.
I hear in the West they think the joker's bad luck, and I kind of get why.
Sometimes the joker saves your skin, and sometimes it's the last thing you want.
In short, it's an almighty card you can use any way you like.
People hate anything they can't pin down. It's instinct.{p}

...What?
What do cards have to do with stories about school, you ask?
Hey, don't rush me.
I'm about to start the story.
There's a guy in my class named Kazuo Okura.
That guy really knows how to get ahead in the world.
Knows how to get ahead, or, like, he's crafty... okay, to put it plainly, he's a real stickler about money.
Me, I'm more on the easygoing side, so I don't even really count how much is in my wallet.
Even if you worry about money, you just end up spending it right away, right?
{a}, what about you?{p}Are you careful with money?
I'm careful with it
Not really

People like that had better watch out.
They end up needing Okura's services.{p}

Okura, see, runs a loan-sharking business at school.
And he's making a killing off it.
It's a crime, of course.
Not something anyone should get away with.
But a lot of people use him, you know.
And when I say loan shark, I don't just mean he lends money and collects interest.
He runs all kinds of dirty rackets at school.
Everything from buying and selling goods to doing homework for hire to running the gambling.
As for goods, they say anything you want, whether it's a computer or a pair of skis, you can get it cheap if you ask Okura.
Though supposedly it's all shoplifted.
And the really amazing part is his gambling racket.
Can you guess what it's like?{p}

Say a fight breaks out somewhere, right?
Then he sets odds on who'll win and gets everybody to bet.
And he pockets the take.
Does he ever lose money, you ask?
Nope, not Okura.
Seems those fights are rigged.
The two doing the fighting are in on it, and who wins in the end is scripted from the start.
So he can switch the ending to whichever one pays Okura the most.
It's a fight in name only. It's really a show.
Well, everybody enjoys watching the show, so call it an admission fee.
So he's rolling in cash.
Do the delinquents shake him down? Not really.
He makes enough to hire bodyguards with it.
When I think about what he'll be like as a grown-up, it scares me.
But I bet he'll turn into one hell of a businessman.
Anyway, on to his real business, the loan-sharking.
Whoops, his real business is supposed to be studying...
He is a student, after all, technically.
Well, let's not be so uptight about it.{p}

You know what a loan shark is, right?
It's a business where you lend money, tack high interest onto it, and get it paid back.
Ever heard of "ten-in-ten"?
Ten-in-ten means charging ten percent interest every ten days.
And if you can't pay that interest, it gets added onto the principal you first borrowed, and the debt keeps snowballing. That's how it works.
Okura's ruthless.
He lends money at ten-in-ten, after all.
He even gets a proper signed IOU.
And what comes next is the real kicker.
He deliberately doesn't collect the interest.
First he comes up to you all smiles and lends you money, right?
Then the borrower goes to pay him back on the agreed date.{p}

And then, for some reason, Okura vanishes.
So they can't pay him back.
The days just keep slipping by, and once it's swelled to an amount they can't possibly repay, that's when he goes to collect.
With his bodyguards in tow.{p}

You don't hear of anything this ruthless even in the adult world, right?
So even the delinquents at the nearby schools treat Okura with respect.
There are even rumors he's become something like a shadow boss.
You watch out for Okura too.
He's got a good nose.
Once he sniffs out someone who's broke, he pops up out of nowhere and quietly creeps up on them.
And then he makes them a sweet offer.{p}

"Hey there.
Short on cash?
I'll lend you some, real cheap."
...Like that.
Which brings us to the cards.{p}

Okura's a huge gambling fan.
I mean, he even stages those rigged fight shows himself.
Life's basically one big gamble anyway, right?
It's funny, but watching Okura, I really believe that saying.
And he's especially crazy about cards.
Say poker or blackjack and he comes running.
I heard him say it once.
"I make money so I can gamble."
That's what he said.
But he's bad at it.
Hopelessly bad, Okura is.
Maybe that's why nobody had come to hate him yet.
He takes those high rates on his loans, but he's terrible at gambling.
He's got no luck when it counts.
So all the money he worked to make, he coughs right back up.
And so everybody figures it's fine if he takes high interest, since they can win it right back.
The world works out pretty neat, huh?
"Money goes around and around," like they say. Truer words were never spoken.{p}

How about it?
{a}, do you like gambling?
I like it
I hate it

I see.
{f:Guys|That's}{f: are all like that| a little unexpected}.{p}
{f:Basically,|At a glance,}{f: nobody hates gambling| you don't seem the type for it, though}.{p}

Then let me ask you one more thing.
Are you any good at gambling?
I'm good at it
I'm bad at it

Wow, look at you.
{f:Calling yourself good like that,|Dunno where you gamble, but}{f: you're either really good| if you flat-out say you're good,}{f: or just full of yourself.| you must be pretty skilled.}
...Whoa, whoa, don't get all starry-eyed,
{a}.
After hearing about Okura just now, you weren't thinking of making him your mark, were you?
Okura being an easy mark is ancient history.
He was harmless enough back when he was lousy at gambling.
But one day, out of nowhere, he got good.{p}

Like he'd turned into a different person.
From then on, Okura was totally possessed by money.
He got even harsher about collecting debts, and the sums he dealt in kept getting bigger.
And almost every day he'd round people up and play poker in a corner of the classroom.
Though the crowd around him was always the same faces.{p}

I peeked at them playing poker just once.
Apparently, under the official rules, poker doesn't use the joker.
Though there are all kinds of poker rules, so I don't know the details myself.
The poker they were playing had the joker in it.
I was just watching idly, but when I looked closer, I noticed it was a strange deck.
You know how the backs of playing cards often have a pattern or a picture on them?
That picture was creepy.{p}

It was a picture of a woman's face, half of it a skeleton.
Split right down the middle, and the left half was a bare skull.
And the right half was a woman with a cold-looking blue face.
It was a sick picture.
Where on earth do they sell cards like that?
I was curious, so I asked.
"Hey, Okura.
Where'd you buy those cards?"{p}
And what do you think he said?
An antique shop
Dad's gift from abroad
A festival stall
He found them

"This...?
It's a souvenir from my old man.
He bought it in some country somewhere."
Pretty curt answer, that.
Maybe he was focused on the game, but it was like I wasn't even there.{p}

I watched the game for a while.
And then I noticed something strange.{p}

The joker in that deck was a skull.
And a black snake was coiled through the holes of its eye sockets.
It was a creepy joker.
But what was even stranger was that the joker always ended up in Okura's hand.
See, in poker, the joker's an almighty card you can use as anything.
Have just one of those, and you've got a big edge in the game.{p}

So Okura won by a landslide.
But isn't that strange?
By any odds, there's no way the joker always lands in Okura's hand.
Not unless he's cheating.
And since Okura always won, nobody was happy about it.
A few people took him on to try and beat him, but it was no use.
He cleaned them out of every cent they had, and that was that.
So rumors started that he was cheating.
Naturally, the people who hung out with him knew about the rigged fights too, so of course they'd be suspicious.
But you've got to catch a cheater in the act.
Everyone knew the joker would always land in his hand when they played poker, but nobody could figure out the secret.{p}

Besides, ever since he got that deck, Okura wouldn't use any other cards, and he wouldn't take the joker out either.
Naturally, nobody played poker with Okura anymore.{p}So what do you think Okura did?
Desperately hunted for poker partners
Went hard on loan-sharking
Stopped coming to school

He threw himself into his real business, loan-sharking.
Can you figure out why?
To force the people who couldn't pay their interest into playing poker with him.
And the terms were something else.
If you beat Okura at poker, he'd wipe out your whole debt.
But there's always a catch to a sweet deal.
What do you think happened if you lost?
He said you had to hand over your soul when you died.
Everybody laughed.
Even if you lost, all you had to do was write down, "I'll give you my soul when I die."
And on top of that, if you wrote it, you got a nice bonus: you could repay the debt whenever you liked.
In other words, for the people borrowing, it meant they practically never had to pay the money back.
Plenty of people jumped at it.
Though the serious types wouldn't even look at it.
And naturally, I didn't give it a second look either.
I mean, think about it.
Even as a joke, how could you write "I'll give you my soul"?
What is this, a pact with the devil?{p}

As soon as they'd borrowed all they could, they'd challenge him to poker.
I mean, losing didn't cost them anything.
All they had to do was take the money and keep him company at poker.
Everybody was pretty casual about it.{p}

Okura never lost.
Well, the other side wasn't taking it seriously, so it was never much of a contest to begin with.
Everybody thought it was a laugh and wrote up contracts with the devil.
Okura looked happy, sitting in front of the pile of contracts he'd collected.{p}

It was a few days after that.
I'd stayed late at school on some errand.
Well, don't ask me why.
I've got my own stuff going on.
That's when I saw a figure in a corner of the classroom, huddled up like it was hiding.
I wondered who it was and went closer, and it turned out to be Okura.
"Okura."
Okura seemed startled by my voice.
But I was the one who got the shock.{p}

Because he was holding a knife.
When he turned around, he was frantically trying to hide something.
But he was too late.
I saw it.{p}What do you think I saw?
The cards
The contracts
I don't know
Those cards.{p}

Well, to be exact, not the cards.
It was the half-skull woman painted on the backs of the cards.
I couldn't believe my eyes.
How could something like this happen?
That woman had come right out of the cards!
It was disgusting, I tell you.
And I say woman, but it was just a head.
About the size of a ping-pong ball, and it looked kind of like a shrunken head.
And there was nothing below the neck.
Well, not nothing; under the neck it was covered in tiny tentacle-like things, all squirming and wriggling.
It walked by moving those tentacles.{p}

"Shindo! Don't look!"
Okura threw himself over them to hide them.
But there was no way he could hide them all.
And I was frozen stiff. I couldn't even move my eyes.
What do you think Okura was doing?{p}

He'd cut the pads of his fingers with the knife and was feeding them his blood.
Tiny women's heads were sucking on all five of Okura's fingers.
It was a grotesque sight.
Half of each face was a pure-white skull, right?
And yet the other half was smiling happily, like the blood tasted that good.
Eyes narrowed, half rolled back to the whites.
"These things can't live unless they eat people.
I'm out of time.
I need the souls of fifty-three people, no matter what!"
That's what Okura was screaming.
Maybe I was caught in those women's spell, because I couldn't move a single step.{p}

"Shindo! Please!
Die for me!"
The fingers of Okura's left hand had those women's heads gnawing on them, right?
And he raised the knife in his right hand at me.
That's when I came back to my senses.
It felt like the women's spell had broken.
"Stop it!"
I shoved Okura away as hard as I could.{p}

"Stop it!
You'll get your food, like we agreed!
As long as I've got these contracts, you'll never run short of food!
The food isn't m......"
Okura couldn't get away anymore.
The women were swimming happily in the pool of blood gurgling up out of his belly.{p}

"Aaaaaaaaaargh!"
I let out a scream and ran for it like a madman.{p}

I don't remember what happened after that.
I killed Okura.
Even now, I can still see it.
...What happened to Okura after that, you ask?
Strangely enough, the bloodbath I saw in that classroom was gone without a trace, all cleaned up as if nothing had ever happened.
Okura was listed as missing.
He wasn't at home either.
He just vanished from in front of everyone, out of nowhere.
Though I'm the only one who knows the real reason.{p}

...But you know, lately I've been thinking.
Maybe it was all just an illusion.
At least let me believe that.
Otherwise, I'm a murderer, you know?
I don't know what those women were.
I bet that deck of cards was their home.
And normally they lie in wait, plastered flat against the backs of the cards.
Though I've got no idea where those cards or the contracts are now.
But what's going to happen to the people who signed those contracts back then?
Eating a soul... how do you even eat one?
Did Okura vanish from this world without even leaving a body because his soul got eaten?
If it really happened, and those women ran off with everyone's contracts...{p}

No, let's not think about that.
What kind of deal Okura made with them doesn't interest me, either.
It's just, even now, whenever I play cards, I make sure to take a good look at the picture on the back.
If that picture's a creepy one...
I'll tear that deck to pieces, no question.{p}And that's the end of my story.
...So now it's the last one, huh?
Let's hear it.{p}

That's no way to answer.
Here I am, going to the trouble of talking to you.
Even just to be polite,
"I like them"
is that so hard to say?
I'll ask you one more time.{p}{a}, do you like playing cards?
I like them
I hate them

"You're a boring {f:guy|one}, you know that?
I was going to tell you a story about cards, but forget it."
{f:I|I} panicked.
"{f:I'm sorry|I'm sorry}, Shindo.
Please, go on with your story."
Shindo glared at {f:me|me}.{p}

"...Maybe I'll reconsider.
But just telling it the normal way is no fun.
How about we let these decide what I tell you?"
As he said it, he pulled a deck of cards out of his pocket.
Carrying those around with him... {f:did he really love cards that much?|he must really love cards.}{p}

"{a}, pick one of these.
If it's the ace, I'll tell you the card story like I planned.
If it's the king, you get a different story.
And if it's the joker..."
Shindo's eyes seemed to glint.
"I'll tell you a story that's been passed down at this school, a seriously dangerous one.
So, which one are you gonna pick?"{p}
Which card should I pick?
Left
Middle
Right

Heh, the ace, huh?
Looks like you've got some pretty strong luck.{p}

Whoa, the king.
All right then, I'll tell you a different story.{p}
...Do you like going against what other people say, like you did a minute ago?
I do
Not really

...I see.
So you're a pretty nasty piece of work.{p}

But you'd better watch yourself.
If you're going to defy people, you'd better be ready for what comes with it.
One way or another, payback might come around someday.
Is it weird, me saying something like that?
...Yeah, I guess it is.
But there's a reason for it.
I had a friend, a guy called Ishikawa.
{f:Just like you, he was a real contrarian|That guy was a real contrarian}.{p}

Friends, parents, teachers, it didn't matter, he never once just went along with what anyone told him.
Normally a guy like that gets shut out by everyone, right?
But not Ishikawa.
That was because he had a certain secret.{p}...What do you think it was?
He could tell when people would die
He could pull anything out of thin air

That's right, he could tell when people were going to die.
Nobody wants to die, right?
I guess they figured if they got friendly with him, he'd warn them when they were in danger.
If you know ahead of time, you can dodge it.
I don't think you can blame them for that.
The one to blame was Ishikawa, no question.
If he says he won't tell you, or that he'll lie to you, you're gonna get scared, right?
He threatened people like that and did whatever he wanted.
But there was one teacher who didn't believe what Ishikawa said.
And what do you think the guy said then?
"You die instead of my grandma, teacher!"
...That's what he said.
Of course, the teacher just laughed it off.{p}

But the next day, that teacher died.
A sudden heart attack, or so I heard.
And in exchange, apparently, Ishikawa's grandma, who'd been bedridden, got better.
Can you believe it?
If that's true, then Ishikawa could even swap people's lifespans.
A guy like him having a power like that... honestly, it was criminal.
Everyone thought so, but nobody could say it out loud.
Then one day, it happened.{p}

Ishikawa's face was paler than I'd ever seen it.
One of his hangers-on went over to ask him why.
The kid came back white as a sheet.
"I-Ishikawa says he's found out when he's going to die.
He says it's tonight."
That was a huge shock.
Think about it, the guy could control people's lifespans★
If he knew he was about to die, who knows who he'd pick to die in his place.
For once, everybody pulled away from Ishikawa, like the tide going out.
Nobody wanted to get caught in the crossfire.{p}

When I looked, there was Ishikawa, standing in the hallway.
His eyes were drawn up, wild and terrifying.
He was looking for someone to die in his place!
Everyone knew it right away.
So nobody could leave the classroom.
If Ishikawa's eyes landed on you, you were done for.
No way was I having that either.{p}

So I slipped out through the window.
Our classroom was on the second floor, after all.
But Ishikawa spotted me on the way.
"Shindo☆"
He yelled and came after me.
It's embarrassing, but I was scared.
Scared out of my mind, I ran right out of the schoolyard.
Ishikawa kept coming after me.{p}

"Die instead of me☆"
He screamed it out of nowhere.
The person's eyes went wide.
It was a man in work clothes.{p}
As I recall, the man eyed Ishikawa like he was some kind of nutcase and hurried off.{p}

Ishikawa just stood there dumbfounded too.
I guess he never meant to dump it on a total stranger.
But still, this meant he wasn't going to die anymore.
He got a little of his cool back and stood there glaring at me.{p}

But that night, Ishikawa died.
They say the worst people live the longest, but with Ishikawa, that turned out to be wrong.{p}

Shindo finished his story, looking satisfied.
"W-wait a minute.
I mean, couldn't this Ishikawa guy swap lifespans{f:...?|...}★"
{f:I|I} asked, confused.
If he could, then why did he die{f:?|?}
Shindo watched {f:me|me}, grinning.
"Don't get it?
Then here's a hint.
That stranger at the school gate... the work clothes he had on were from a well-known motorcycle courier company."
What {f:was he getting at|did he mean}?
I didn't get it at all.
Shindo shook his head at {f:me|me} as if he pitied me.{p}

"Jeez, you still don't get it?
Ishikawa died in a traffic accident.
He ran out into the road and got hit by a courier's motorcycle."
A motorcycle courier★
"Th-then the person who swapped lifespans with Ishikawa was..."{p}

"That's right, it was the guy he crashed into.
Of course, he died too.
Of all people, Ishikawa swapped lifespans with the one guy who was going to die right along with him."
Shindo laughed, enjoying himself.
The story seemed a little too neat, but the way Shindo was delighting in it didn't look like an act.
Well, {f:I guess these things happen|maybe these things do happen}.{p}"Thank you very much."
{f:I|I} bowed to Shindo.
Then I turned to the sixth person.{p}

Yeah, he could pull anything he wanted out of thin air.
A kind of psychic power, right?
So there were always people crowded around him.
Everyone trying to get him to conjure up the manga or CDs they wanted.
Pathetic, huh?
Me, I wasn't about to go wagging my tail at him.
I just watched from a distance.
I'd be lying if I said I wasn't jealous at all, though.
There were a fair number of people besides me who kept away from him too.{p}

One of them was a girl.
Uchida, I think her name was.
The quiet, pale type who sat out a lot of gym classes.
Apparently she really did have a weak heart.
She was kind of cute, and she drew people's eyes.
How do I know so much about her?
Well, see, Ishikawa fell for her.
For Uchida.
He'd even go out of his way to use his powers right in front of her.
It was totally obvious.
But she didn't show the slightest interest.
Ishikawa got more and more frustrated.
And finally, he made up his mind to talk to her directly.{p}

But Ishikawa had never really gone out with a girl before.
The moment he opened his mouth, it was,
"If there's anything you want, I'll make it appear for you."
...Right out of the blue, just like that.
Uchida must have been taken aback.
"No... I'm fine, thank you."
"Don't be like that, there must be something, right?"
Ishikawa kept pressing her.
But Uchida kept turning him down.
That's when he lost his temper.
"You think I'm lying.
You think there's no way I could do something like that!"
"N-no, that's not..."
"If you don't believe me, I'll bring out whatever you treasure most!
Then you'll have to believe me!"
Uchida frowned.
I guess he took that to mean she still doubted him.{p}

Ishikawa gripped his right wrist with his left hand and started to focus his mind.
Beads of sweat broke out on his forehead.
He was desperate too.
A guy wants to look good in front of the girl he likes.
{f:You'd be the same, right?|You know how it is, right?}
...And while he was doing that, Uchida started acting strange.
Her face, always bloodless, went even paler, the color of paper.
She was breathing hard and dripping with greasy sweat.
But Ishikawa didn't notice.
He focused every nerve in his body on his right hand.
And then, the moment his concentration hit its peak...{p}

A slimy, glistening red lump, just about the size of his palm.
Was that fresh blood dripping from it★
Every time it gave a twitching jerk, warm red liquid gushed out of the torn, tube-like things sticking out of it.
Someone screamed again.
He could hear footsteps running up from all directions.
Ishikawa looked down at Uchida lying on the floor.
She was clutching the left side of her chest, her face twisted in pain, but she wasn't breathing anymore.
Of course she wasn't.
By then, even Ishikawa was starting to understand what had happened.{p}

Do you get it, {a}?
...That's right.
With his psychic power, Ishikawa had pulled Uchida's heart right out of her.
For someone as frail as Uchida, the thing she treasured most was her own heart.
Some psychic power, huh?
No, maybe I should call it a wonderful power, since it brought out exactly what he asked for.{p}

...What happened to Ishikawa after that?
He moved away right after.
So I couldn't tell you.
But I did see him right before the teachers took him away.
He was in a daze, like his whole personality had fallen apart.
He'd held the heart of the girl he loved in his hand.
That'd be a shock.
He'll probably never forget it as long as he lives.
...Yeah, I don't think I'll ever forget that sight either.{p}

Hmm, I see.
Well, that's for the best.
Why, you ask?
Because if you're going to defy people, you'd better be ready for what comes with it.
One way or another, payback might come around someday.
Is it weird, me saying something like that?
...Yeah, I guess it is.
But there's a reason for it.
I had a friend, a guy called Ishikawa.
That guy was a real contrarian.{p}

Whoa, if it isn't the joker.
Then I'll tell you the one I've been saving.{p}

A scary, creepy, seriously intense one.
Are you ready for it?
I'm ready
I'm not ready
Good, then I'll tell you.{p}

Have you all noticed what's here right now?
I don't mean the ones sitting in their seats, quietly listening to the seven wonders.
I mean the ones that snuck in while we've been sitting here talking.
...Come on, don't make that weird face.
You say nobody came into this room?
That's right, not in any form you can see.
But they're here.
{a}, you look like you've got a strong sixth sense.
You'd be able to tell, wouldn't you?
Talk about stuff like this at this school, and of course they're going to gather.
Well, most of them just drift around and can't lay a finger on people.
But some of them are powerful.
What if I told you one of them was watching you... would you believe me?{p}

Hahaha, your face has gone stiff.
You're scared after all, huh?
Of course you are.
Nah, sorry, sorry.
Shindo was grinning.{p}Had {f:I|I} just been {f:messed with|teased}?
Protest that it's mean
Quietly put up with it

"If that's what you think... I'll show you proof it wasn't.
Give me your hand."
"Huh...?"
{f:I|I} stared blankly at the hand Shindo held out, looking like an idiot.
He clicked his tongue at {f:me|me} in irritation.
"Give it here, I said.
If you go on not noticing, you're the one who's in danger.
I'm lending you my power."
{f:I|I} timidly held out my hand.{p}

{f:What is this|What is this}★
Shindo quickly clamped his hand over {f:my|my} mouth as I was about to scream.{p}

The thing was already gone.
Was it because I'd let go of Shindo's hand{f:?|?}{p}

"I told you not to be startled.
Provoke it the wrong way and there's no telling what it'll do to you."
Saying that, Shindo pulled away.
"Wh-what was that..."
"The one I told you about earlier.
Looks like it's taken a liking to you."
"N... no way!"
As {f:I|I} panicked, Shindo gave me a cold look.
"That's what you get for setting up a project like this half for fun.
You're the one who called it here.
That thing's gonna follow you around from now on."
"No way!
Isn't there some way to get rid of it★"
"Sorry, I don't know any.
I've just got a bit more of a sixth sense than most people, that's all."
Shindo grinned.{p}

{f:I|I} was annoyed, but I kept quiet.
He was my senior, after all{f:.|.}
Shindo saw {f:me|me} like that and gave a wry smile.
